So I can say I'm a coffee addict. I have always used drip machines or French presses. However, I heard about this pour over coffee technique and was curious.
This product is actually pretty amazing. The same coffee grinds that I use in my drip pot, I used in here. Wow, what a difference in flavor! After following the directions and letting the grinds bloom, the rest of the process was a breeze. The coffee came out better than I have ever tried. It was quicker than making a whole pot and clean up was easy. Just dump out the grinds in the trash and rinse it in hot water. I recommend this to anyone who enjoys a really good cup of coffee.

I don't drink a ton of coffee, but I like a cup or two in the morning. This pour-over coffee maker is perfect for my needs. Just slowly pour hot water (just off boiling) over some fresh, coarsely ground beans and watch the magic happen. The coffee is delicious and mellow, and the clean-up is a breeze. I also appreciate being able to be more environmentally conscious by not buying disposable coffee filters.

The filter is very well made and feels solid, as does the included spoon. A PDF recipe book is included as well.

Compared to a filter that uses paper cones, the water tends to go through the coffee much quicker, so the resulting coffee is very light. I have to re-run the water/coffee through it at least three times to get something similar to a paper cone filter. Considering this, I wouldn't use this filter on a daily basis and probably keep it around as a spare.
Love the product! It works great, just like expected. Seems to be made of good quality. I did not get the free recipe book as promised.

I chose between two options: copying my brother by ordering a cheap, plastic dripper and using paper filters or spending 3x the cost of the cheap plastic dripper and not needing paper filters. I chose the higher quality, stainless steel dripper, which I am reviewing right now.

Not only does it come with a handy-dandy (stainless steel?) scooper, but I won't be worrying about (1) scolded plastic getting into my coffee and body, regularly buying new filters, or finding filters that aren't unhealthy with dyes and whatnot.

The perceived disadvantage is that this filter, compared to the plastic/paper combo, restrains the flow of water through the coffee at a faster pace and, perhaps, not allowing enough coffee-water time. I don't notice a difference in the taste though.

I would recommend this to anyone. The cost between the plastic and this dripper is about $7 --> $20... So, consider the cost of paper filters over the longevity of the item.

I was a bit weary at first about how the coffee would taste since I would let the coffee steep for three to five-ish minutes using the press compared to the one minute needed for the drip, but it tastes just as delicious and the experience feels more personal in an odd yet satisfying way.

This is a beautiful, simple and effective way to prepare a delicious cup of coffee. Unfortunately, the top ring, by which you hold it and remove it from the mug, completely separated from the funnel and base after only a month of use. So when it's hot, there is no handle or way to grasp it to remove it from the mug. Aside from that unfortunate craftsmanship, it's a great piece. Another nice design element is that there are cutaways in the metal at the bottom, so after the coffee drips through the filter, you can see it go into the mug and clearly see how full the mug is without removing it entirely.

After about 10 uses it no longer works like it did when new.  The water hardly flows through and it now takes a long time just to get half a cup of coffee before the water flow stops altogether.  I've cleaned it thoroughly several times, still no use.  I'm tossing it in the garbage.
